tagline: A loop through hunt country, where even the hedges hunt.
intro: From Cockeysville the loop heads west on Shawan Road into what is called Hunt Country, crosses the Worthington Valley, runs up MD 128 by Butler, then east by Hereford and Monkton into Harford County and back south past Loch Raven Reservoir to Glen Arm and Towson. Fox hunters have crossed these fields since colonial times, followed by the hill toppers, who prefer to watch and ride at a slower pace.
On Thanksgiving morning the Greenspring Valley Hounds meet at St. John's Church in the Worthington Valley for the Blessing of the Hounds.

moments.title: Worthington Valley
moments.text: The Maryland Hunt Cup runs four miles over 22 timber fences here, and an English trainer asked about bringing a horse over said, "Why I wouldn't dare."

moments.title: Ladew Topiary Gardens
moments.text: Harvey Ladew, socialite and huntsman, gave his gardens a fox hunt in clipped topiary, horses, riders, hounds and foxes all clearing a hedge.

moments.title: Hampton National Historic Site
moments.text: The Ridgelys raced horses from this estate north of Towson, and free and enslaved Black men worked as their jockeys and grooms out of the 1805 stable.
